zxv.name: MODE
zxv.signature: MODE(m as UByte, w as UInteger = 0, h as UInteger = 0)
zxv.doc: MODE n[, w, h]: mode 0 (256 x 192, 32 x 24 characters) or 1 (512 x 384). In mode 0 the page can be bigger than the screen (512 x 384, 1024 x 192 or 256 x 768), and SCROLL moves the screen over it. Both pages are cleared, page 0 is shown and drawn on, and the scroll, REMAP, PALETTE and CLIP go.

zxv.name: PAGE
zxv.signature: PAGE(n as UByte)
zxv.doc: PAGE n: the page that is shown (0 or 1)

zxv.name: SCREEN
zxv.signature: SCREEN(n as UByte)
zxv.doc: SCREEN n: the page everything draws on. Drawing on the hidden one and then showing it gives animations without flicker.

zxv.name: SCROLL
zxv.signature: SCROLL(x as Integer = 0, y as Integer = 0)
zxv.doc: SCROLL x, y: the pixel (x, y) of the page is seen at the top left corner of the screen; SCROLL alone puts it back

zxv.name: REMAP
zxv.signature: REMAP(c as UByte, n as UByte)
zxv.doc: REMAP c, n: colour c is seen as n, at once and on all the screen

zxv.name: REMAPRESET
zxv.signature: REMAPRESET
zxv.doc: REMAPRESET: every colour as it was (REMAP with no arguments)

zxv.name: PALETTE
zxv.signature: PALETTE(c as UByte, r as UInteger, g as UInteger, b as UInteger)
zxv.doc: PALETTE c, r, g, b: colour c (0-15) is seen with that red, green and blue (0-255 each; 215 is the level of the standard colours, 255 the bright one), the nearest one ZX-V shows, at once and on all the screen

zxv.name: PALETTERESET
zxv.signature: PALETTERESET
zxv.doc: PALETTERESET: the standard colours again (PALETTE with no arguments)

zxv.name: WAIT
zxv.signature: WAIT(n as UInteger = 1)
zxv.doc: WAIT [n]: until the next frame, and until n frames have gone since the last WAIT: a steady pace for games

zxv.name: GRAB
zxv.signature: GRAB(n as UByte, x as Integer, y as Integer, w as UInteger, h as UInteger, t as Integer = -1)
zxv.doc: GRAB n, x, y, w, h[, t]: sprite n (0-255) is that rectangle of the drawing page; colour t becomes transparent

zxv.name: GRABSTR
zxv.signature: GRABSTR(n as UByte, w as UInteger, ByVal a$ as String)
zxv.doc: GRABSTR n, w, a$: sprite n from a string, a character a pixel and w pixels a row: the hex digits are the colours, anything else (".", " ") is transparent

zxv.name: SPRITE
zxv.signature: SPRITE(n as UByte, x as Integer, y as Integer, f as UByte = 0, ByVal c$ as String = "", w as UInteger = 0, h as UInteger = 0)
zxv.doc: SPRITE n, x, y[, f[, c$[, w, h]]]: draws sprite n with its top left corner at (x, y). f: 1 mirrored left to right, 2 upside down, 3 both. c$ changes its colours: colour i is drawn as the hex digit i of c$ (any other character leaves it). w, h: stretched or shrunk to that size.

zxv.name: HIT
zxv.signature: HIT(a as UByte, ax as Integer, ay as Integer, b as UByte, bx as Integer, by as Integer) as UByte
zxv.doc: HIT(a, ax, ay, b, bx, by): 1 if a solid pixel of sprite a at (ax, ay) falls on a solid pixel of sprite b at (bx, by); it draws nothing

zxv.name: BOX
zxv.signature: BOX(c as UByte, x as Integer, y as Integer, w as Integer, h as Integer)
zxv.doc: BOX c, x, y, w, h: a filled rectangle of colour c

zxv.name: DISC
zxv.signature: DISC(c as UByte, x as Integer, y as Integer, r as Integer)
zxv.doc: DISC c, x, y, r: a filled circle

zxv.name: POLY
zxv.signature: POLY(c as UByte, x1 as Integer, y1 as Integer, x2 as Integer = -32768, y2 as Integer = 0, x3 as Integer = -32768, y3 as Integer = 0, x4 as Integer = -32768, y4 as Integer = 0, x5 as Integer = -32768, y5 as Integer = 0, x6 as Integer = -32768, y6 as Integer = 0, x7 as Integer = -32768, y7 as Integer = 0, x8 as Integer = -32768, y8 as Integer = 0)
zxv.doc: POLY c, x1, y1[, x2, y2...]: a point, a line or a filled polygon (up to 8 points)

zxv.name: PATTERN
zxv.signature: PATTERN(n as UByte = 0, p as Integer = -1)
zxv.doc: PATTERN n[, p]: BOX, DISC and POLY draw with pattern n (1 to 11, as PATTERN in the BASIC of ZX-V: 1 a chessboard, 2 a quarter, 3 an eighth, 4 three quarters, 5 and 6 stripes, 7 and 8 diagonals, 9 a grid, 10 bricks, 11 diamonds): their colour where the pattern has a 1, and paper p (0-15) where it has a 0, or nothing there with p = -1 (the default). PATTERN alone (or 0): no pattern. Needs a ZX-V ROM with patterns (ZX-V D110)

zxv.name: PATTERNBITS
zxv.signature: PATTERNBITS(r0 as UByte, r1 as UByte, r2 as UByte, r3 as UByte, r4 as UByte, r5 as UByte, r6 as UByte, r7 as UByte, p as Integer = -1)
zxv.doc: PATTERNBITS r0, r1, r2, r3, r4, r5, r6, r7[, p]: a pattern of your own, a byte a row (BIN 10101010...; bit 7 is the pixel on the left), with paper p as in PATTERN

zxv.name: CLIP
zxv.signature: CLIP(x as Integer = 0, y as Integer = 0, w as Integer = -1, h as Integer = 0)
zxv.doc: CLIP x, y, w, h: the fast graphics only draw in that rectangle; CLIP alone, everywhere

zxv.name: PIXEL
zxv.signature: PIXEL(x as Integer, y as Integer) as Byte
zxv.doc: PIXEL(x, y): the colour (0-15) of a pixel of the drawing page, whoever drew it; -1 out of the page

zxv.name: KEY
zxv.signature: KEY(n as UInteger) as UByte
zxv.doc: KEY(n): 1 if the key is down now (several at once). n: CODE "a" to CODE "z", CODE "0" to CODE "9", 8 to 11 the cursor keys (left, right, down, up), 12 Backspace, 13 Enter, 32 Space, or 256 + a USB key code

zxv.name: JOY
zxv.signature: JOY(n as UByte) as UInteger
zxv.doc: JOY(n): the buttons of joystick n (0 or 1); 0 if it is not connected. 1 right, 2 left, 4 down, 8 up, 16 fire 1, 32 fire 2, 64 fire 3, 128 start, 256 select

zxv.name: SOUND
zxv.signature: SOUND(r as UByte, v as UByte)
zxv.doc: SOUND r, v: writes v in register r of the AY chips (0-15 the first, 16-31 the second)

zxv.name: TIME
zxv.signature: TIME as ULong
zxv.doc: TIME: the frames (60 a second) since the machine started

zxv.name: MUSICLOAD
zxv.signature: MUSICLOAD(ByVal f$ as String)
zxv.doc: MUSICLOAD f$: loads a module (without an extension, the first there is of f$.zxm, f$.pt3, f$.vgm and f$.vgz): ZX-V's own .zxm (the two AY chips and the sample channels: what zxv-music makes of a MOD, S3M or XM), Pro Tracker 3 or Vortex Tracker II (.pt3, what zxv-tracker saves), a TurboSound (two modules, one on each AY chip), Pro Tracker 2, Sound Tracker, ASC Sound Master, a PSG dump or a VGM of AY chips (.vgm, or compressed: .vgz, which takes 32 KB more to play). It goes in the heap.

zxv.name: MUSICPLAY
zxv.signature: MUSICPLAY
zxv.doc: MUSICPLAY: plays the module in the background while the program goes on, and at its end goes back to its loop position, for ever. It plays on the first AY chip (a TurboSound, on both), until MUSICSTOP or the end of the program.

zxv.name: MUSICSTOP
zxv.signature: MUSICSTOP
zxv.doc: MUSICSTOP: stops the music

zxv.name: MUSICPAUSE
zxv.signature: MUSICPAUSE
zxv.doc: MUSICPAUSE: silences the music; MUSICCONTINUE goes on where it was

zxv.name: MUSICCONTINUE
zxv.signature: MUSICCONTINUE

zxv.name: MUSIC
zxv.signature: MUSIC as UByte
zxv.doc: MUSIC: 1 while the music plays, 0 if not

zxv.name: SFXLOAD
zxv.signature: SFXLOAD(ByVal f$ as String)
zxv.doc: SFXLOAD f$: loads an AYFX bank of sound effects (without an extension, f$.afb: what the effects tab of zxv-tracker or the AY Sound FX Editor saves), or a single effect (.afx). It goes in the heap.

zxv.name: SFX
zxv.signature: SFX(n as UByte, c as Byte = -1)
zxv.doc: SFX n[, c]: plays effect n of the bank (the first is 0) without waiting, on a free channel of the chip the music does not use, or on channel c: 0 to 2 are A, B and C of the first chip and 3 to 5 those of the second

zxv.name: SFXSTOP
zxv.signature: SFXSTOP
zxv.doc: SFXSTOP: stops all the effects

zxv.name: SFXPLAYING
zxv.signature: SFXPLAYING as UByte
zxv.doc: SFXPLAYING: 1 while any effect plays

zxv.name: SAMPLELOAD
zxv.signature: SAMPLELOAD(ByVal f$ as String, n as UByte)
zxv.doc: SAMPLELOAD f$, n: loads a WAV (without an extension, f$.wav) as sound n (0 to 31) in the sound memory: 8 or 16 bits, mono or stereo, at any rate, and with its loop if it has one (a smpl chunk). Nothing stays in the RAM.

zxv.name: SAMPLE
zxv.signature: SAMPLE(n as UByte, tone as Float = 0, vol as UByte = 64, pan as UByte = 128, c as Byte = -1)
zxv.doc: SAMPLE n[, tone, vol, pan, c]: plays sound n without waiting, tone semitones up (or down, negative: 12 is an octave), with its volume (0 to 64) and pan (0 left, 128 centre, 255 right), on a sample channel the music does not use, or on channel c (0 to 11). A sound with a loop goes on until SAMPLESTOP.

zxv.name: ZXVSAMPLEPLAY
zxv.signature: zxvSamplePlay(n as UByte, mul as ULong, vol as UByte, pan as UByte, c as Byte)

zxv.name: SAMPLESTOP
zxv.signature: SAMPLESTOP(c as Byte = -1)
zxv.doc: SAMPLESTOP [c]: stops the sound of channel c, or all of them

zxv.name: SAMPLEPLAYING
zxv.signature: SAMPLEPLAYING as UByte
zxv.doc: SAMPLEPLAYING: 1 while any sound of SAMPLE plays

zxv.name: TILE
zxv.signature: TILE(s as UByte, n as UInteger, x as Integer, y as Integer, w as UInteger = 0, h as UInteger = 0, t as Integer = -1)
zxv.doc: TILE s, n, x, y[, w, h[, t]]: tile n (0-4095) of the set of side s (8 or 16) is the s x s square of the drawing page at (x, y); with w and h, that rectangle cut in tiles numbered from n row by row. Colour t becomes transparent. A set grows when a higher tile is defined (the new ones, black)

zxv.name: TILESTR
zxv.signature: TILESTR(s as UByte, n as UInteger, ByVal a as String)
zxv.doc: TILESTR s, n, a$: tiles from a string, s x s characters each (the hex digits are colours, anything else transparent); a longer one defines the next tiles

zxv.name: MAPDIM
zxv.signature: MAPDIM(m as UByte, w as UInteger, h as UInteger, s as UByte = 8, r as UByte = 0)
zxv.doc: MAPDIM m, w, h[, s[, r]]: map m (0-15) of w x h cells, all tile 0, of tiles of side s (8 or 16); with r = 1 it repeats in both directions

zxv.name: MAPPOKE
zxv.signature: MAPPOKE(m as UByte, x as UInteger, y as UInteger, v as UInteger)
zxv.doc: MAPPOKE m, x, y, v: cell (x, y) is v: the tile, + 4096 mirrored left to right, + 8192 upside down, + 16384 its 8 transparent, + 32768 priority

zxv.name: MAPPOKESTR
zxv.signature: MAPPOKESTR(m as UByte, x as UInteger, y as UInteger, ByVal a as String)
zxv.doc: MAPPOKESTR m, x, y, a$: the cells from (x, y) to the right, the code of each character as the tile: "  ##.." uses tiles 32, 35 and 46

zxv.name: MAP
zxv.signature: MAP(m as UByte, mx as Integer = 0, my as Integer = 0, x as Integer = 0, y as Integer = 0, w as Integer = -1, h as Integer = -1, f as UByte = 0)
zxv.doc: MAP m[, mx, my[, x, y, w, h[, f]]]: draws map m from its pixel (mx, my) on the whole page or the rectangle (x, y, w, h); f: 0 every cell, 1 the ones without priority, 2 only the ones with it. All its tiles must exist

zxv.name: CELL
zxv.signature: CELL(m as UByte, x as Integer, y as Integer) as UInteger
zxv.doc: CELL(m, x, y): the cell at column x and row y of map m, with its bits; out of a map that does not repeat, 0

zxv.name: TEXTURE
zxv.signature: TEXTURE(n as UByte, x as Integer, y as Integer, s as UInteger, c as Integer = -1, t as Integer = -1)
zxv.doc: TEXTURE n, x, y, s[, c[, t]]: texture n (0-3) for FLOOR and ROTATE is the s x s square (2, 4, 8... 256) of the page at (x, y). It repeats or, with colour c, outside it is that colour; colour t is transparent, and with c = t, the outside too

zxv.name: FLOOR
zxv.signature: FLOOR(n as UByte, x as Fixed, y as Fixed, height as Fixed, angle as Fixed, horizon as Integer, focal as Fixed = 0)
zxv.doc: FLOOR n, x, y, height, angle, horizon[, focal]: a floor in perspective with texture n (the "mode 7"), seen from its point (x, y) at that height, looking at angle (radians; 0 towards the growing x), with the horizon at that row of the page and that focal length (0: half the page; smaller, wider)

zxv.name: FLOORMAP
zxv.signature: FLOORMAP(m as UByte, x as Fixed, y as Fixed, height as Fixed, angle as Fixed, horizon as Integer, focal as Fixed = 0)
zxv.doc: FLOORMAP m, x, y, height, angle, horizon[, focal]: the same with tile map m (what is out of a map that does not repeat is not drawn)

zxv.name: ROTATE
zxv.signature: ROTATE(n as UByte, x as Fixed, y as Fixed, angle as Fixed = 0, zoom as Fixed = 1, cx as Integer = -32768, cy as Integer = -32768)
zxv.doc: ROTATE n, x, y[, angle[, zoom[, cx, cy]]]: texture n turned angle radians clockwise and zoom times bigger around its point (x, y), which is seen at (cx, cy) of the page (by default its centre), on the whole page or the CLIP

zxv.name: ROTATEMAP
zxv.signature: ROTATEMAP(m as UByte, x as Fixed, y as Fixed, angle as Fixed = 0, zoom as Fixed = 1, cx as Integer = -32768, cy as Integer = -32768)
zxv.doc: ROTATEMAP m, x, y[, angle[, zoom[, cx, cy]]]: the same with tile map m
